text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in 5xx + timeouts for /api/v1/generate (us-west-2). Error rate ~9% over last 5m, p95 latency ~2.4s, several gateway timeouts. Affected routes: /v1/generate (default model), /v1/chat. See console: https://console.redwood.example/incidents/5173337777

devon: taking this — oncall Devon here. Allocating now.

devon: quick situational checks:
```
# health
curl -sS https://ingress-usw2.redwood.example/health | jq .status
# tail recent errors
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=batcher-scheduler -c batcher --tail=200 | grep -i "timeout\|5xx" | tail -n 50
```

devon: Observed batcher queue depth spike on scheduler-3. backlog ~28k requests, avg batch size increased from 4 -> 26, worker CPU pinned on 3 nodes. Many older requests stuck waiting on a single long-running KV-prefetch job causing front-of-queue lock. Not classic HOL wording but a frontlock — early requests are delaying new low-latency traffic.

mike: customer-impact note: noticed elevated 502/504 for a small set of high-traffic customers (acct-42, acct-77). Support already got piled alerts. ETA on mitigation?

amber: oncall SRE Amber here — first mitigation: enable routing fallback to lightweight model variant and open an emergency ingress throttle. Steps I propose now: 1) enable model-fallback policy to route non-critical requests to rwd-mini-llama; 2) increase batcher-worker replicas on scheduler-3; 3) kill stuck prefetch tasks. Doing in that order to reduce customer pain.

devon: doing 1 & 2 now. Running scale and toggle: 
```
kubectl -n inference scale deployment batcher-scheduler-3 --replicas=8
rdctl routing set-fallback --route /api/v1/generate --fallback rwd-mini-llama --region us-west-2 --duration 15m
```

devon: toggled fallback, scaled batcher up. Starting to see drop in p50 for new requests, but backlog still draining slowly.

amber: issuing targeted eviction of long-running prefetch jobs: 
```
kubectl -n inference exec -it batcher-scheduler-3-0 -- bash -c "ps aux | grep prefetch | awk '{print $2}' | xargs -r kill -9"
```

mike: confirmed acct-42 error rate dropped from 18% -> 6% after fallback. Still seeing intermittent 504s.

devon: enabled an emergency ingress throttle to limit tokens per-request to 6k for non-enterprise tier, using rate-limiter rule id `rl-203`. This should cut tail latency and stop huge batches forming.

elaine: product: posting a short customer-facing note to status page: "We are investigating increased error rates and timeouts affecting text generation; mitigation in progress. Some requests are being routed to a lower-latency model to reduce errors." Will coordinate messaging once we have clearer ETA.

amber: diagnostic snapshot: stack traces and scheduler metrics show a KV prefetch loop for oversized contexts causing worker threads to block for 10-20s — this amplifies with large batch sizes. Root trigger looks like an unexpected distribution of token lengths from a small set of clients.

devon: temporary filter applied to drop requests with >12k tokens from free tier, and we set `batcher.max_batch_time_ms=80` for the affected pool to avoid long-wait batching.

incident-bot: :information_source: Note: automatic anomaly detection created alert rule `ingress/5xx-spike` at 5173337810.

mike: customer impact update: support has queued outreach for top 10 impacted accounts. No revenue-critical customers in the hit list, mostly heavy experimentation.

devon: handing off to next oncall Lina for overnight monitoring. Handoff summary: scaled batcher replicas to 8, fallback to rwd-mini-llama active until 2026-03-16T04:30Z, ingress throttle rule rl-203 active, stuck prefetch processes killed, batcher.max_batch_time_ms lowered. Key indicators to watch: ingress 5xx %, queue backlog, scheduler CPU, avg batch size. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.example/frontlock-runbook

lina: taking over. I will keep fallback active for another 30m and watch for regression. If backlog doesn't reduce to <2k in next 20m, plan is to spin up a second scheduler pool in us-west-2 and shift 40% of traffic there.

amber: agree. If shifting traffic, ensure we set `route_quality: conservative` to avoid saturating the new pool. Also please collect a sampling of offending requests for eval — we need a long-term fix to refuse oversized context tokens or progressive prefetch.

lina: acknowledged. I'll also patch a temporary metric alert to catch `batcher.avg_wait_ms > 120` to trigger early paging.

devon: thanks team. Leaving a short log dump attached to the incident page; I'll pop back if anything spikes. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: RESOLVED (auto): routing fallback + scale + throttle reduced 5xx to baseline. Final metrics: error rate returned to 0.7% within 17 minutes, p95 latency back under 900ms. Incident record: https://console.redwood.example/incidents/5173337777/summary

elaine: product note updated on status page: "Mitigations in place; majority of users restored. Follow-up: investigating oversized-context patterns and throttling policy changes."

lina: will create a follow-up ticket to harden prefetch and add input-size guardrails. Assigned to @amber and @devon.

mike: closing loop with support to confirm outreach done.

devon: good handoff. Signing off.
